sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 9.1% a year from FY2016 to FY2025, rising from $23.7 billion to $51.8 billion [F1][F10][F168].
The path was cyclical rather than steady: revenue fell 58.0% in FY2020 to $13.7 billion, then rose 153.2% in FY2021 and 76.5% in FY2022 to $61.0 billion [F5][D161][F6][D200][F7][D238].
The FY2022 jump came mainly from higher realized commodity prices and higher sales volumes, primarily from the Shell Permian acquisition [P59].
Since the FY2022 peak revenue has slipped, with a 20.5% decline in FY2023 and a 5.3% three-year CAGR to FY2025 [F7][F8][D274][D844].
The U.S. is the core: it was 79.1% of FY2025 revenue and contributed 5.7pp of the 4.9% growth [D382][D384][D342].
Crude oil was 66.3% of FY2025 revenue but added only 0.1pp of growth, while natural gas added 4.4pp on 37.4% growth [D551][D553][D586][D585].
FY2025 sales and other operating revenues rose $4.2 billion on higher volumes of $6.2 billion, including Marathon Oil volumes, partly offset by lower realized crude prices [P28].
Profit did not keep pace: net income fell 13.6% in FY2025 against 4.9% revenue growth, and EPS fell 18.7% [D343][D342][D344].
The diluted share count rose 6.1% in FY2025, so EPS fell faster than net income [D356][D343][D344].
Net margin was 15.4% in FY2025, below the 17.9% window median and far under the 30.6% FY2022 high [F30][D831][D830].
Cost of revenue rose to 37.9% of revenue from 36.6%, and D&A rose to 19.5% from 17.5% [D326][D292][D330][D296].
DD&A increased $1.9 billion in FY2025, primarily from the Marathon Oil acquisition and higher production volumes [P22].
SG&A fell $265 million, mainly the absence of $545 million of Marathon transaction expenses, partly offset by restructuring severance [P23].
The effective tax rate rose to 36.9% from 32.4%, widening the gap between operating and net margin [D332][D298].
Operating cash flow of $19.8 billion was 2.48x net income in FY2025, above the 2.07x window median [F59][F20][D333][D855].
The FY2025 decline from $20.1 billion in FY2024 came from lower commodity prices, mostly offset by Marathon Oil operations [P6][F58][F59].
Operating cash flow was 33.6% of revenue, and capex of $10.2 billion in FY2022 was 1.35x D&A [D331][F66][D228].
Stock-based compensation was only 1.7% of operating cash flow, so it does not distort conversion [D334].
Cash and investments were $8.1 billion at FY2025, up 13.4%, against $1.0 billion of current debt [D335][D357][X203].
The current ratio was 1.30x, below the 1.45x window median [F153][D843].

FY2025 uses of cash were $12.6 billion of capex and investments, $5.0 billion of buybacks, $4.0 billion of dividends and $0.9 billion of debt retirement, partly offset by $3.2 billion of asset sales [P7].
Buybacks plus dividends of $9.0 billion were 46% of operating cash flow, above the stated 30% framework [D339][F59][P31].
Revenue in the table is a later recast, not the first-reported figure: FY2025 shows $51.8 billion against $58.9 billion in that year's 10-K [F10][X10].
Growth and margin comparisons across recast and never-recast years mix two presentations, so the arc figures should be read with that caveat [R1].
Long-term debt is not reported after FY2020, so net cash and debt growth cannot be tracked into FY2025 [R6][F157].
Short-term investments are missing for FY2021, so cash and investments and net cash omit them that year [R7][X183][X184].
Net margin: a move back above the 17.9% window median would reverse the FY2025 decline, while a drop below the 15.4% latest level would confirm it [D831][F30].
Operating cash flow: holding at or above the $19.8 billion FY2025 level would confirm the cash trend; falling below it would reverse it [F59].
Diluted share count: a fall back below the 1,253.4 million FY2025 level would reverse the 6.1% dilution, reported in the next 10-K [X131][D356].
